text.aria-label: Title text 'Figure 5: Restoring removed calendar inputs raises wind forecast loss for July 2025–June 2026'
text.tspan: Figure 5: Restoring removed calendar inputs raises wind forecast loss
for July 2025–June 2026

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'XGBoost tree models train on April 2024–June 2025; forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026. Each XGBoost model uses 500 squared-error trees, maximum depth 6, and learning rate 0.05. Each tree samples 80% of rows and can use all columns. These training and scoring dates define Fold A. All scored forecast times are included. The reduced wind-input baseline retains 16 of the full control’s 24 real inputs. Each plotted comparison adds one removed input to that baseline. All input sets use corrected wind and radiation processing. Duplicate retained inputs keep all XGBoost models at 24 training columns. Weekday ordinal is a day-of-week number. Weekday and time-of-year sine and cosine encode weekly and annual cycles. Squared-error models fit each meter separately. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble. Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is better. The fair-CRPS correction assumes independent draws; its use with weather-ensemble values is diagnostic. Each plotted comparison uses matched forecasts and observations and weights wind meters and three random-seed fits equally. A seed sets the random choices in a training run. Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or transfer to new meters. The eight planned 95% intervals are unadjusted for multiple comparisons. This panel does not test differences between the added inputs. The loss increase is statistically significant at the unadjusted 5% level for six of the eight additions under the primary month-and-seed intervals. Dew-point temperature and downward short-wave radiation differences remain unresolved under the primary intervals. Individual effects cannot be added together to explain the full-input versus reduced-input loss difference. Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Frozen capacity is used only for scoring. Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one matched training seed. Negative differences mean lower loss after adding the named feature to the reduced wind-input recipe. All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.'
text.tspan: XGBoost tree models train on April 2024–June 2025; forecasts are scored July 2025–June 2026.
Each XGBoost model uses 500 squared-error trees, maximum depth 6, and learning rate 0.05. Each tree samples 80% of
rows and can use all columns.
These training and scoring dates define Fold A. All scored forecast times are included.
The reduced wind-input baseline retains 16 of the full control’s 24 real inputs. Each plotted comparison adds one
removed input to that baseline.
All input sets use corrected wind and radiation processing. Duplicate retained inputs keep all XGBoost models at 24
training columns.
Weekday ordinal is a day-of-week number. Weekday and time-of-year sine and cosine encode weekly and annual cycles.
Squared-error models fit each meter separately. Each power forecast contains 51 values, one from each alternative
weather prediction supplied by the weather ensemble.
Continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) compares the forecast power distribution with observed power; lower is
better.
The fair-CRPS correction assumes independent draws; its use with weather-ensemble values is diagnostic.
Each plotted comparison uses matched forecasts and observations and weights wind meters and three random-seed fits
equally.
A seed sets the random choices in a training run.
Ranges describe variation across whole months and individual fits, rather than uncertainty in the three-fit mean or
transfer to new meters.
The eight planned 95% intervals are unadjusted for multiple comparisons. This panel does not test differences
between the added inputs.
The loss increase is statistically significant at the unadjusted 5% level for six of the eight additions under the
primary month-and-seed intervals.
Dew-point temperature and downward short-wave radiation differences remain unresolved under the primary intervals.
Individual effects cannot be added together to explain the full-input versus reduced-input loss difference.
Frozen capacity is each meter’s full-history 99th percentile of absolute power, including later readings. Frozen
capacity is used only for scoring.
Dot: mean loss difference on matched forecasts. Line: 95% interval from repeated draws of whole months and one
matched training seed.
Negative differences mean lower loss after adding the named feature to the reduced wind-input recipe.
All rows are planned: written into the study plan before any result existed.
